stories.title: Capgemini raises its 2026 outlook for the second time on AI work
stories.summary: Capgemini reported third-quarter revenue of 6.07 billion euros, up 11.7 per cent at constant currency, helped by the WNS and Cloud4C acquisitions and AI-led projects. It raised its full-year growth target to 9 to 9.5 per cent, from about 8.5 to 9. It is the second upgrade this year.

stories.title: Accenture lets AI agents screen its job applicants
stories.summary: Accenture uses AI agents to screen resumes, schedule interviews and run skills assessments, with humans making final hiring decisions, HR chief Kate Clifford told an investor day. The firm calls it 'frictionless recruiting' and reports faster hiring. Critics cite research questioning the fairness of AI recruitment.

stories.title: KPMG Australia's former leaders keep millions despite docked pay
stories.summary: A whistleblower scandal cost KPMG Australia's former chief executive Andrew Yates and ex-chairman Martin Sheppard more than $1.2 million in docked pay and bonuses. Yates still collected $6.7 million in earnings and retirement payouts after forfeiting almost $700,000. Sheppard took home $1.8 million after a $526,000 bonus cut.

stories.title: EY Ireland's revenue grows 4.4% to 880 million euros
stories.summary: EY Ireland reported revenue of 880 million euros on the island of Ireland for the year to June 2026, up 4.4 per cent from 843 million. Headcount stood at more than 5,600, and the firm now has 158 equity partners across the island.

stories.title: KT Nambi takes over as Capgemini's India business head
stories.summary: KT Nambi has become managing director of Capgemini's India Business Unit, succeeding Ananth Chandramouli, who moves to lead Insights and Data for Asia-Pacific and the Middle East. Nambi, a 15-year Capgemini veteran across two stints, said he will focus on clients, partners and turning opportunities into measurable outcomes.

stories.title: KPMG forensic report finds outsiders behind Capillary's diverted payments
stories.summary: KPMG's forensic investigation into a Capillary Technologies subsidiary found that four fraudulent payments totalling 3.04 million euros were diverted by external actors using domain spoofing and executive impersonation. The report ruled out insider collusion, internal system breaches and employee involvement.

stories.title: BearingPoint's North America joint venture turns one
stories.summary: BearingPoint and ABeam Consulting are marking the first anniversary of BearingPoint North America, their Chicago-based joint venture set up in September 2025. It builds on an alliance dating to 2011 and offers SAP and AI-driven enterprise transformation for clients across the Americas, Europe and Asia.

stories.title: McKinsey finds 76% of Indian shoppers use AI to buy online
stories.summary: A McKinsey survey of about 21,000 shoppers in 11 markets found 76 per cent of Indian consumers use AI tools to look up products, compare options or guide purchases. That puts India second only to China, at 80 per cent, and well ahead of the global average.

stories.title: KPMG's India CEO Outlook finds bosses confident and buying cyber defences
stories.summary: The KPMG 2026 India CEO Outlook finds CEOs in India confident about growth despite geopolitical volatility and regulatory complexity. They are raising spending on cybersecurity, digital risk management and operational resilience. The AI agenda is shifting from adoption to measurable value, the report says.

stories.title: Gartner says 44% of CEOs struggle to show returns from AI
stories.summary: Forty-four per cent of CEOs struggle to demonstrate financial returns from AI to stakeholders, a Gartner survey of 203 global CEOs and senior executives found. Yet 75 per cent plan to increase technology investment. Gartner says adding more AI to existing workflows will not solve the problem.

stories.title: BCG says critical minerals belong on the boardroom agenda
stories.summary: Critical mineral supply risks are rising as demand grows and supply stays concentrated in a handful of countries, BCG Johannesburg partner Tycho Moencks told Mining Weekly. BCG's report flags overlooking smaller-volume but essential materials, and poor visibility beyond direct suppliers, as blind spots for companies.

stories.title: Kearney forecasts global supply chain costs rising 2.7 to 6.7%
stories.summary: Kearney's latest Supply Chain Navigator forecasts global supply chain costs rising between 2.7 and 6.7 per cent, with big differences by country and US costs up as much as 5 per cent. Geopolitical risk rose 64.5 per cent globally, and container rates climbed 6.8 per cent.

stories.title: McKinsey finds crews and hangars now limit Asia's business jet charter
stories.summary: McKinsey's first State of Business Aviation report counted a record 3.9 million business jet departures worldwide in 2025. Alongside a Honeywell outlook, it suggests crews, hangar space, maintenance slots and airport access, not aircraft, now constrain charter growth in Asia. The jets are ready, the parking is not.

stories.title: Roland Berger says satellites are becoming mobile network rivals
stories.summary: Satellite-native companies in the US are acquiring mobile spectrum and building hybrid space and ground networks to compete directly with mobile operators, a Roland Berger study says. It argues the shift reaches beyond coverage to the economics, sovereignty and competitive structure of mobile markets.

stories.title: Only 36% of wealthy Indian families have documented succession plans
stories.summary: A Grant Thornton Bharat and Entrust Family Office study of families with wealth of roughly Rs 100 crore to Rs 10,000 crore found only 36 per cent have documented succession plans. Still, 54 per cent said succession is becoming an ongoing planning process, not an automatic inheritance.

stories.title: Blue Matter buys healthcare communications agency Cognite
stories.summary: Blue Matter, a life sciences strategy consultancy backed by Baird Capital, has acquired Cognite, a healthcare strategy and communications agency, from Vespa Capital for undisclosed terms. Cognite has offices in the UK, Switzerland and the US and specialises in complex markets including rare diseases.

stories.title: India's PE and VC inflows jump 46% to $17.1 billion in Q3
stories.summary: Private equity and venture capital investment in India reached $17.1 billion in the third quarter of 2026, up 46 per cent from $11.7 billion a year earlier, the EY-IVCA roundup shows. Deal volumes fell 9 per cent to 348, as large transactions drove the total.

stories.title: Tata Motors appoints Deloitte Haskins and Sells after B S R resigns
stories.summary: The Tata Motors board on 31 October accepted the resignation of its statutory auditors, B S R and Co. LLP, and approved Deloitte Haskins and Sells LLP as the new auditors to fill the casual vacancy. The appointment is subject to shareholder approval.

stories.title: India's pharma and healthcare deals hit a record 87 in Q3
stories.summary: India's pharma and healthcare sector recorded 87 deals worth $4.3 billion in the third quarter of 2026, a quarterly high by volume, Grant Thornton Bharat's Dealtracker shows. Values were lower than the previous quarter, which included Sun Pharma's $11.75 billion acquisition of Organon.

stories.title: NIIT Learning Systems picks PwC's Price Waterhouse as its auditor
stories.summary: NIIT Learning Systems' board has recommended Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP as statutory auditors for five years from 2027 to 2032, subject to shareholder approval. Current auditor S. R. Batliboi and Associates LLP will leave after the 25th AGM in 2027.

stories.title: Australian Ethical drops KPMG as auditor after 13 years
stories.summary: Fund manager Australian Ethical has shelved KPMG as its external auditor after 13 years and opened a competitive tender for audits from FY28. It said the decision followed scrutiny of KPMG's audit practices, including by a parliamentary committee. Chair Steve Gibbs said the firm had served it well.

stories.title: EVERSANA buys London's Estima Scientific for AI health economics
stories.summary: EVERSANA has acquired Estima Scientific, a London health economics and outcomes research company, to expand its AI-powered commercialisation work for drugmakers. Estima's generative AI tools handle economic modelling, literature reviews and network meta-analysis, and its consultants will join EVERSANA's market access team.

stories.title: Englobe to acquire Calgary's Obsidian Engineering
stories.summary: Englobe has agreed to acquire Obsidian Engineering, a Calgary firm offering engineering, procurement and construction management services, adding more than 400 professionals. Obsidian has delivered more than 3,500 projects across energy and data centre markets. A corrected version of the announcement was later issued.

stories.title: Oddball buys Synaptic's Salesforce business
stories.summary: Federal digital services provider Oddball has acquired Synaptic Era's Salesforce technology and services business, adding Salesforce, Agentforce and AI government modernisation skills. It is Oddball's first acquisition since an investment from Falfurrias Management Partners in December 2024. Synaptic has completed more than 600 Salesforce projects.

stories.title: TPM Holdings refocuses on AI and Salesforce after buying Hunley
stories.summary: TPM Holdings has completed an 18-month realignment around AI and Salesforce for architecture, engineering, construction and manufacturing clients. It includes its March 2026 purchase of The Hunley Group, a Salesforce and AI consulting partner, which now sits with TrebleHook under TPM CRM Solutions.

stories.title: Maine Pointe teams up with supply chain software firm Sophus
stories.summary: Charlotte supply chain consultancy Maine Pointe has formed a strategic partnership with Sophus Technology of Ann Arbor. It will pair its consulting and implementation work with the Sophus X platform, which uses digital twins, scenario analysis and optimisation to help clients test network decisions before committing capital.

stories.title: KPMG Bermuda hires Sean Duffy as a tax partner
stories.summary: KPMG in Bermuda has appointed Sean Duffy as a partner in its tax practice, succeeding Jay Payne, who is retiring after more than 30 years. Duffy brings more than 25 years of experience in the United States advising public and private companies on tax compliance and governance.

stories.title: GST process reforms for small sellers take effect from 1 November
stories.summary: Simplified GST registration for small sellers on e-commerce platforms, unified registration documents, faster refunds and easier rules for post-supply discounts roll out in phases from 1 November. The 57th GST Council meeting on 8 October approved the changes, mainly covering registration, returns and refunds.

stories.title: Finance ministry estimates Q2 growth at 7.35%
stories.summary: India's economy grew an estimated 7.35 per cent in the July to September quarter, the Finance Ministry's October Monthly Economic Review says, citing strong domestic demand, industrial activity and consumption. The nowcast follows 7.8 per cent growth in April to June and beats the ministry's earlier 7.3 per cent projection.

stories.title: World Bank brief says India lifted 496 million out of poverty
stories.summary: India lifted 496 million people out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, as the share below the lower middle income poverty line fell from 57.7 to 16.1 per cent, according to the World Bank's October 2026 Poverty and Equity Brief. Extreme poverty fell to 2.6 per cent.

stories.title: Ashok Lahiri warns against expansionary policy amid inflation risks
stories.summary: With global inflation firming in food and petroleum and El Nino adding price pressure, a knee-jerk expansionary policy response may not be appropriate, NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman Ashok Lahiri said on Friday. He favoured a cautious approach, speaking at the CII Banking Colloquium.

stories.title: Sebi to publish an FII compliance paper within weeks
stories.summary: Sebi will release a consultation paper on foreign institutional investor compliance within weeks, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said, seeking views on aligning Indian norms with global standards. Foreign investors have withdrawn a net $31.4 billion from Indian equities this year, contributing to a persistent fall in stock indices.

stories.title: Thirteen of 19 services sectors post double-digit growth in August
stories.summary: Thirteen of 19 services sub-sectors recorded double-digit growth in August, up from 10 in July, according to the trial Index of Services Production released by the National Statistical Office. Retail trade led, repair services rebounded sharply and air transport contracted for a fifth straight month.

stories.title: Bengaluru leads India's office rent growth, matching Tokyo
stories.summary: Bengaluru is India's fastest-growing prime office rental market, with annual growth of 11.5 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, matching Tokyo, Knight Frank reports. Demand from multinationals, global capability centres and domestic businesses drove it. Professionals moving to the city may notice the costs too.

stories.title: CBRE says India needs up to 1.5 billion sq ft of private education space
stories.summary: India will need around 1.0 to 1.5 billion square feet of additional private education infrastructure by FY2035, driven by rising enrolment and demand for quality education, CBRE says. It expects expansion across private schools and higher education, and more interest from institutional investors in education real estate.

stories.title: Invest India's CEO gets only a six-month extension
stories.summary: Nivruti Rai, appointed Invest India MD and CEO in July 2023 with a three-year tenure, has received a 'short-term interim extension of six months' until January 2027, government sources told The Indian Express. Some of her key decisions are under scrutiny by auditors, internal committees and Commerce Ministry officials.

stories.title: IIM Bangalore places all 608 students with 128 firms for the summer
stories.summary: IIM Bangalore recorded 100 per cent summer placements for its 2026 to 28 PGP and PGPBA batches, with 608 students taking offers from 128 firms at a median monthly stipend of Rs 2 lakh. Consulting was the biggest segment, with 308 offers from 22 firms, led by Accenture Strategy's 123.

stories.title: IIM Ahmedabad's summer placements offer over 230 roles
stories.summary: IIM Ahmedabad has concluded summer placements for its 2026 to 28 PGP batch, with recruiters offering more than 230 roles across three clusters between 23 and 30 October. Sectors ranged from consulting, investment banking and private equity to consumer goods, technology and renewable energy, in a hybrid format.

stories.title: BCG says AI services work can be staffed from existing payrolls
stories.summary: AI-led services could generate $100 billion to $200 billion in net new work by 2030, and technology services firms can meet much of it by reskilling their existing staff, a BCG report says. Its title is 'The Talent Is Already on Your Payroll. The Clock Isn't.'

stories.title: Fewer IIT and IIM graduates are founding startups in 2026
stories.summary: Just 79 IIT alumni and 20 IIM alumni founded technology startups between January and August 2026, against 307 and 71 in all of 2025, Tracxn data shows, Mint reports. The figures are not directly comparable, it notes, while startup formation overall keeps climbing.

stories.title: Built In lists firms hiring operations consultants
stories.summary: Operations consultants, who help businesses cut procurement costs and fix logistics snags, earn an annual base salary of around $92,000, Built In says, as companies rebuild fragile supply chains. Its list of firms actively hiring includes Boston Consulting Group, Accenture, Deloitte, Bain and Company and Kearney.

stories.title: What an MBA in AI leads to in 2026
stories.summary: An MBA in AI can lead to management roles such as business intelligence director, AI product manager and AI strategy consultant at global technology and consulting firms, a careers guide says. It argues demand is high for people who can connect machine learning with business operations.
